rows.claim: The file header says the roster carries 'the three-part admission'. Spec §11.3 'Device identity and admission' says 'Admission is a two-part check at the attach point, in order (D-375)': identity, then claims.
rows.evidence: design/spec.md:8441-8452 (two-part, AlreadyAttached then ClaimConflict); design/log.md:15836 (D-375 'Admission is a two-part check'); log.md:3758 and 6938 are the older three-part forms. Code: src/sim.jl:2512-2523 does identity, then claims.
rows.fix: Replace 'the three-part admission' with 'the two-part admission'.
rows.note: D-375 narrowed the check from identity, affinity, claims to identity, claims.

rows.claim: The raise site throws DeviceContractMismatch with reason :no_loop. The spec's Appendix C entry says 'what the contract lacks: the loop method, the output side ..., or the roster entry a detached handle ... no longer has'. It names no `reason` symbols, while BindingContractMismatch lists all nine of its reasons. The kind has three reasons, :no_loop, :no_output_side and :detached.
rows.evidence: src/diagnostics.jl:1841-1844 (reason::Symbol, :no_loop | :no_output_side | :detached); src/roster.jl:235-236; design/spec.md:15803-15807 (no reasons named); spec.md:15799-15801 lists the Binding reasons; rg for no_loop in design/spec.md finds nothing.
rows.fix: Append to the DeviceContractMismatch entry of Appendix C: 'A `reason` tells the cases apart: `:no_loop`, `:no_output_side` and `:detached`.'

rows.claim: The DataPlane docstring says 'the §11.3 freeze itself is the lifecycle's :running state (devices.jl)'. The freeze is Control's `running` flag (control.jl:70), read by `lifecycle` in sim.jl, and devices.jl holds neither.
rows.evidence: src/control.jl:33-40 and 70; src/sim.jl:511-513 (lifecycle reads control.running); rg 'lifecycle(' src/devices.jl finds nothing; design/code_map.md:270-271 puts the gates in sim.jl.
rows.fix: Write '(control.jl's `running` flag, read by `lifecycle` in sim.jl)' in place of '(devices.jl)'.

rows.claim: The DataPlane docstring says 'the inline body's entry leaves when that body returns, under wake's lock, since the loop reads the registry as it publishes'. No code removes a single entry from run_tasks. The only writes are the fill at spawn and `empty!` at run end. Every device runs in a spawned task and the loop runs on the calling task, so no inline device body exists.
rows.evidence: rg run_tasks src/: sim.jl:1750 (empty! under lock), sim.jl:1809 (fill), sim.jl:2834 (read), roster.jl only; src/sim.jl:1468-1469, 1508, 1652 (loop on the calling task, one task per live entry, D-310); design/log.md:12092 (the old calling-task inline body, superseded).
rows.fix: Delete the clause 'the inline body's entry leaves when that body returns, under `wake`'s lock, since the loop reads the registry as it publishes'. The registry is read under `wake`'s lock and emptied once at run end.

rows.claim: The ModelState docstring says 't is the float nearest t₀ + k·Δt_frame, as the clock writes it, so a typed decimal on the frame grid matches it from an exact origin'.
rows.evidence: src/frame.jl:157-161 and src/model.jl:820-841 write clock.t from step ends, and I did not trace the arithmetic. No probe covers it.
rows.note: This needs the clock's t computation traced through _step_end and the exact origin. It was not settled within the effort allowed.

rows.claim: The code_map.md ModelState bullet ends 'and the fingerprint, the `Deployment` and the structural layout `Fingerprint`'. This names the fingerprint twice and lists three items. ModelState has two such fields, `deployment` and `layout::Fingerprint`.
rows.fix: Write 'and the `Deployment` and the structural layout `Fingerprint`'.

ok.claim: AbstractDevice: loop is mandatory; init!, shutdown! and unblock! are the optional hooks
A device's identity is its instance; one object holds at most one roster entry
The binding is an attach! argument, never a device field
is_input and is_output are Bool traits, false by default
TableBinding is the shipped data-driven binding
No side, a declared side without its method, or a method under a false trait is BindingContractMismatch
is_input returns Bool, false unless the type defines a method
claims without the input side is refused as BindingContractMismatch
reads without the output side is refused as BindingContractMismatch
is_greedy is false by default; a greedy claim is every root input not yet claimed
The greedy claim is computed once at attach, never recomputed, so attachment order decides it
An empty greedy remainder is legal and warns EmptyGreedyClaim
Greedy without the input side, or with claims defined, is BindingContractMismatch
claims returns face names as strings or symbols, called once at attach
Duplicates in a claim collapse
An empty claims collection is a legal claim to write nothing
A non-greedy input binding with no claims method is BindingContractMismatch at attach
An unknown face is AttachUnknownFace; a face another device claims is ClaimConflict
reads returns a NamedTuple of selectors; a non-NamedTuple or non-selector value is BindingContractMismatch
attach! calls reads once and resolves it against the build
A selector with an unknown component path is PathResolution; any other unresolved selector is ReadResolution
The keyword method reads(; selectors...) builds a read set that series takes
check_binding detects defined-but-undeclared with one which against the fallback, and a greedy front end with a gather is legal
check_device refuses a device with no loop before it is rostered or spawned, as a fail-fast DeviceContractMismatch
RosterEntry holds device, id, drain thunk, should_abort, account and handle
The id is monotonic per Simulation, never reused, and assigned on admission only
The binding, the writer over the claim and the diagnostic cell are the handle's
_handle reads the entry's handle with a typeassert to the DeviceHandle family
The drain thunk is zero-argument, captures store and writer concretely, and the drain is allocation-free
_no_drain throws InternalInvariant and is the sentinel until a door or roster change compiles a thunk
The harness cell and account survive roster changes while the writer is recompiled
run_tasks is the run's device-id to Task registry, filled at spawn and emptied at run end
A device absent from run_tasks reads :done inside a run and :none outside one
DataPlane compiles no thunk at construction; harness_drain holds _no_drain until a door or roster change
_claim: greedy is the unclaimed complement; returned claims are validated with AttachUnknownFace, deduplicated, empty allowed
reclaim! rebuilds the exclusivity index and harness writer, reshapes the pending harness batch and discards newly claimed faces as ClaimedFaceEntry
_writer_schemas lists rostered devices in attachment order, then harness
_install_writers! is reached from init!, restore!, replay! (via _open_run!) and from reclaim!'s callers attach! and detach!
_install_writers! appends the writer set to trc.schemas, with a local range, and recompiles every thunk; with no trace the indices are provisional
Control fields and defaults: pace Inf, margin 0.002, stopped true, paused false, running false
stop_issuer is set by a first-wins CAS from nothing
The stop word is cleared at run start and at init!
paused: set and cleared by pause!/resume!; resume! notifies wake; the tail clears it; a run's start never does
running spans run!/step! including the tail and lifecycle derives from it
counter counts published boundaries, mirrored under the lock after the release-store of latest, never re-armed
pace and margin are written by pace!/margin! and by run!/replay! at entry; the loop reads them at frame top
join_timeout is validated at materialization and fixed for the simulation's life
_request_stop!: first CAS wins, then notify under the lock
wait_resume! parks while paused and no stop is pending, returns whether it parked
Pacer is created by the run body and passed to the loop, never a field
anchor! sets the pair (t, τ()) under pace p and clears the debt
reanchor! counts the cleared debt as forgiven and bumps reanchors
wait_deadline!: forgives debt past 5·h/p with DebtReanchor on the loop cell, else hybrid sleep-then-spin; reads each knob once; no wait after an anchor
PacerStatus(pacer) copies the eight fields in order
Fingerprint holds sizes, root faces, paths, x/s/m types, sorted addrs and events as described
ModelState fields x, s, m, table, prior, stepper, t, t₀, deployment, layout
stepper is nothing for RK4/Heun, and under BS3 the proposal and memory as two Float64s
== on a ModelState is identity, so compare fields by value
ok.evidence: rg '==\(' for Fingerprint or ModelState finds no method in src/

ok.claim: Checkpoint is a Float64 ModelState with frame and boundary; checkpoint(sim) returns it
_restore_state! copies every field back, writes t and t₀ and hands the stepper its state, with no discontinuity notice
_restore_stores! writes the s and m stores, shared with linearize
_detach copies mutable fields; deployment, fingerprint and stepper state ride as is
_check_addresses! reports cells and types first, then offsets only if those agree, named port.<name>
_walk_deployment! names the nine parameters, the algorithm field by field, then schedule rows and scopes by path and column
